# Linkedin Post Search Scraper (No Cookies)

The Apify actor [`harvestapi/linkedin-post-search`](https://apify.com/harvestapi/linkedin-post-search) as typed Telo kinds, generated from its build **0.0.114**. The module's version is that build number, and every run it starts is pinned to exactly that build, so the input types below are the ones the actor really runs with.

Search LinkedIn Posts with advanced filters by target profiles or companies. No cookies or account required.

## Pricing

Pay per event — Actor Start $0.00005, Post $0.002, Main profile $0.002, Full profile $0.004, Reaction $0.002, Comment $0.002, 0-result query $0.001 (Free-plan prices; paid plans pay less). Cap the spend with `maxTotalChargeUsd`.

Runs are charged to the Apify account whose token the `ApifyClient` holds. See the [Store page](https://apify.com/harvestapi/linkedin-post-search) for current prices.

## Import

```yaml
imports:
  Actor: oci://ghcr.io/telorun/apify/harvestapi-linkedin-post-search@0.0.114#sha256-…
```

Pin the digest with `telo upgrade`. The module re-exports `ApifyClient`, so it is the only import needed.

## Usage

```yaml
kind: Actor.ApifyClient
metadata: { name: apify }
token: !cel "secrets.apifyToken"
---
kind: Actor.Run          # or Actor.Start for runs longer than 5 minutes
metadata: { name: scrape }
client: !ref apify
maxTotalChargeUsd: 1     # optional: timeout, memory, maxItems, maxTotalChargeUsd
---
kind: Run.Sequence
metadata: { name: main }
steps:
  - name: scrape
    invoke: !ref scrape
    inputs: {}
```

- **`Run`** calls Apify's synchronous endpoint and returns `{ items }`. Apify holds the request open for at most 300 seconds; a longer run fails with HTTP 408.
- **`Start`** starts the run, long-polls it until it finishes, and returns `{ run, items }`. A run that ends `FAILED`, `TIMED-OUT` or `ABORTED` raises `APIFY_RUN_NOT_SUCCEEDED` with the run as `data`.

## Input

Only these fields are accepted — `telo check` rejects any other.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `searchQueries` | array |  |  | Search queries — Queries to search LinkedIn posts. The same query as you would use in the LinkedIn search bar. |
| `maxPosts` | integer |  |  | Maximum number of posts to scrape per each search query — Maximum number of posts to scrape per each search query. If you set this to 0, it will scrape all posts. |
| `postedLimit` | string |  |  | Posted Limit — Fetch posts no older than X time. Options: '1h', '24h', 'week', 'month'. |
| `postedLimitDate` | string |  |  | Posted Limit Date — Scrape posts from now up to and including this date. It supports the [Date time string format](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Date#date_time_string_format). For example, "2011-10-10", or "2011-10-10T14:48:00.000+09:00" or a timest |
| `sortBy` | string |  |  | Sort by — Sort by 'relevance' or 'date'. |
| `authorUrls` | array |  |  | Profile or Company URLs who posted — List of LinkedIn profile or company URLs to scrape. Example: `https://www.linkedin.com/in/williamhgates` will fetch posted or re-posted content by Bill Gates. |
| `authorsCompanies` | array |  |  | Companies where authors work — Scrape posts of profile-authors who assigned to LinkedIn Company Names of these companies. Example: `Google` will fetch posts of Google employees or ex-employees in some cases. |
| `mentioningMember` | array |  |  | Mentioning member — List of LinkedIn profile URLs of members mentioned in posts. Example: `https://www.linkedin.com/in/williamhgates` will fetch posts mentioning Bill Gates. |
| `mentioningCompany` | array |  |  | Mentioning company — List of LinkedIn Company Names mentioned in posts. Example: `https://www.linkedin.com/company/google` will fetch posts mentioning Google. |
| `contentType` | string |  |  | Content type — Filter posts by content type. For example, if you choose 'Videos', it will scrape only posts containing videos. |
| `authorsIndustryId` | array |  |  | Authors industry ID — Scrape posts of profile-authors who assigned to LinkedIn Industry IDs of these industries. Full list: https://github.com/HarvestAPI/linkedin-industry-codes-v2/blob/main/linkedin_industry_code_v2_all_eng.csv |
| `authorKeywords` | string |  |  | Author keywords — Scrape posts of profile-authors whose profiles contain at least one of these keywords in the headline or job title sections. |
| `profileScraperMode` | string |  | `"short"` | Profile Scraper Mode — Choose the mode for scraping LinkedIn profiles. The Short mode provides basic information, while the Full mode includes full detailed profile data. |
| `startPage` | integer |  | `1` | Start Page — The page number to start scraping from. |
| `scrapePages` | integer |  |  | Number of pages to scrape — The number of search pages to scrape. Each page contains 100 posts |
| `scrapeReactions` | boolean |  |  | Scrape Reactions — Scrape reactions of posts. |
| `maxReactions` | integer |  |  | Maximum number of reactions to scrape per post — Maximum number of reactions to scrape per post. Default is 10. |
| `reactionsProfileScraperMode` | string |  | `"short"` | Profile Scraper Mode for reactions — Choose the mode for scraping LinkedIn profiles. The Short mode provides basic information, while the Full mode includes full detailed profile data. |
| `postNestedReactions` | boolean |  |  | Post nested reactions (legacy, not recommended to enable) — Whether to add reactions items inside post items. In a case of hundreds of reactions, the Actor might hit the max item size limit and won't be able to save a post. |
| `scrapeComments` | boolean |  |  | Scrape Comments — Scrape comments of posts. |
| `commentsPostedLimit` | string |  |  | Comments Posted Limit (filter) — Fetch comments no older than X time. Options: '1h', '24h', 'week', 'month'. |
| `maxComments` | integer |  |  | Maximum number of comments to scrape per post — Maximum number of comments to scrape per post. Default is 10. |
| `commentsProfileScraperMode` | string |  | `"short"` | Profile Scraper Mode for comments — Choose the mode for scraping LinkedIn profiles. The Short mode provides basic information, while the Full mode includes full detailed profile data. |
| `postNestedComments` | boolean |  |  | Post nested comments (legacy, not recommended to enable) — Whether to add comments items inside post items. In a case of hundreds of comments, the Actor might hit the max item size limit and won't be able to save a post. |

## Output

The actor publishes no dataset schema, so `items` are untyped objects.
